question: How do HS's designs for a FieldDeck handheld, a camera rover, a small drone and a desktop arm compare with published products and open designs, in function and in design quality?
method: Reference figures are quoted from each maker's page or repository on 2026-11-26 (URL per figure); 'not stated' means the page gave none. HS's side is HS's own existing design or a design HS produced today. Design quality uses HS's own checks; references are judged on published facts only.

hs_design.display: Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2, 7 in, 720 x 1280
hs_design.checks: runtime, supply margin, USB current, print bed fit, display-post bending all pass its own limits; scene_fit: 0 overlaps, designed 0.3 mm seams, keyboard held by unmodelled pads
hs_design.not_done: no thermal or drop validation; nothing built

MNT Pocket Reform.compute: RK3588 (4x A76 2.4 GHz + 4x A55) or QCS6490
MNT Pocket Reform.open: fully open source hardware (schematics and design files public)

ClockworkPi uConsole.compute: swappable cores incl. RPi CM4 4 GB

azlan-works/Argo (CM5 carrier).power: BQ25895 charger with power path, TPS61022 5 V boost up to 3 A
azlan-works/Argo (CM5 carrier).open: CERN-OHL-S-2.0 label; README forbids commercial reproduction without agreement

comparison: Footprint: 310 x 285 mm (883 cm2) against Pocket Reform's 200 x 126 mm (252 cm2): 3.5x the area for the same screen size, 64 vs 45 mm thick.
Runtime: 2.8 h computed against Pocket Reform's stated ~4 h.
Compute and screen: Pi 4B 2 GB and 720p against RK3588 (16 GB option) and 1920 x 1200.
Cost: about US$337 in parts against EUR 1,099+ assembled; every part off the shelf and replaceable, no custom PCB.
Open designs in this class (Argo, PiUPS, Beepy) use a charger with power path and a boost converter; HS buys that function as a power bank, simpler and larger.
fielddeck.verdict: A working, checked digital design of a bulky budget cyberdeck. It is not competitive with Pocket Reform in size, runtime or screen; it wins on cost and repairability.

hs_design.parts: SpeedyBee F405 Mini stack, 4x F1404 3800KV, HQ T3x3x3, M10Q-5883 GPS, 4S 650 mAh
hs_design.thrust_to_weight: about 5:1 from the maker's thrust table
hs_design.checks: mass with density sensitivity, T/W, hover current, battery C-rating, ESC margin, arm stiffness vs rotor band, PyBullet hover/gust/motor-failure scenarios; scene_fit: no real clashes (13 overlaps are stand-in grommets and strap)
hs_design.not_done: nothing built or thrust-stand tested; flight time is an extrapolation

comparison: Against DJI Mini 4 Pro in the same 250 g class: 7-10 min against 34 min, no camera gimbal or long-range link, but an open stack with a 5:1 thrust margin a camera drone does not have.
Its real peer class is 3-inch GPS FPV quads; their maker pages could not be read today (Flywoo 403, BetaFPV 429), so that comparison is still open.
drone.verdict: The most complete HS design (CAD, fabrication files, cited sizing, simulation). Functionally an FPV-class quad, far from a camera drone's endurance; it needs a thrust-stand and a flight to stand behind its numbers.

hs_design.source: robot_arm_design with DeepSeek on the benchmark's blind requirements (380 mm, 0.5 kg, safety factor 1.5)
hs_design.joints: 6 revolute: base yaw, shoulder, elbow, wrist pitch, wrist roll, tool roll; links 80/150/150/60/40/20 mm (500 mm chain)
hs_design.actuators: generic inventory entries (4.0 / 2.5 / 1.0 Nm), not named servos
hs_design.checks: reach upper bound pass; payload-only torque with 1.5x factor pass at every joint (wrist pitch margin 0.12 Nm); link self-weight, workspace, joint limits unresolved
hs_design.second_request: 550 mm / 0.75 kg: rejected by HS's schema because the model gave a wrist joint a 0 mm link
hs_design.motion_check_on_a_real_arm: motion_sweep on SO-101: elbow clear to 84 of its 96.8 degree limit

SO-101.servo: STS3215, 16.5 kg.cm stall at 6 V (7.4 V version)

ROBOTIS OpenMANIPULATOR-X.note: figures from a model-extracted page summary; verify on the page

comparison: Every reference names its actuators and publishes reach, payload and repeatability from a built arm; HS's design names generic torque classes and cannot claim repeatability.

HS's torque check ignores link and servo weight; for SO-101-class arms that weight (about 0.63 kg modelled in its URDF) is comparable to the 0.5 kg payload, so the real margin is smaller than reported (HS says so: LINK_SELF_WEIGHT_TORQUE_UNRESOLVED).
HS's strongest arm capability today is checking an existing arm (the SO-101 joint sweep), not designing one.
robotic_arm.verdict: Proposal stage: the shape is reasonable, the checks are honest about what they skip, but it is not buildable until it picks real actuators and counts self-weight.

hs_design.source: robot_reference_e2e on its indoor inspection rover case (14 selected references from 51)
hs_design.what_it_produced: source graph (47 claims, 0 conflicts), 2-wheel differential topology with lidar, manufacturing cross-checks (pin/firmware identity), 15-step operator guide
hs_design.engineering_numbers: runtime 102 min from a declared 96 Wh battery and 45 W load; 4 A supply margin from declared 15 A / 11 A
hs_design.status: blocked by design (9 blockers): parts and dimensions are declared inputs, not chosen by HS
hs_design.camera: none: the case is a lidar rover, so the CCTV brief has not been run

NVIDIA JetBot.price: less than $150 add-on to Jetson Nano

comparison: The open rovers publish architectures and prices but almost no runtime, speed or camera figures, so the functional comparison has little to compare against yet.
HS's rover planner is strong on traceability and weak on design: it checks declared numbers rather than choosing motors, battery and camera.
cctv_rover.verdict: Least ready of the four for a CCTV rover: no camera, video-streaming or drive sizing yet.

overall: Drone and FieldDeck: complete, checked digital designs, functionally behind the best products (endurance, size) and ahead on openness and cost.
Arm and rover: HS plans and checks but does not yet choose real actuators, motors, cameras or batteries, so their designs are not buildable.
No HS design in this trial has been built or measured.

committed: src/hardware_splicer/data/actuators/cited_servos_20261126.json: Dynamixel XL330/XL430/XM430/XM540 (checked word for word against each ROBOTIS e-manual page), STS3215 (from the SO-ARM100 README; Feetech and Waveshare pages unreadable), MG996R

src/hardware_splicer/data/drive/pololu_gearmotors_20261126.json: Pololu micro metal HP 6V, 25D HP/MP 12V, 37D 12V, every ratio, with the maker's torque limits and the 25% of stall current rule (spot-checked against the raw pages)
src/hardware_splicer/data/actuators/joint_actuator_comparison/: 87 families of robot joint actuators, CC BY 4.0, copied unchanged with attribution
local_only: UIUC Propeller Database zip (90.9 MB, 264 static files): its pages state no licence, so HS reads it from where the user downloads it
not_obtained: Feetech's own STS3215 page and Waveshare's ST3215 wiki (403)
ESP32-CAM camera specs (AI-Thinker page had none)

new_tools: arm_actuator_sizing (static stretched-arm torque with actuator weight; pick from cited servos or joint actuators)
drive_sizing (rover gearmotor ratio against Pololu limits)
prop_static (hover rpm and shaft power from UIUC data)
robot_arm_design now accepts a 0 mm wrist link

robotic_arm.hs_design_with_real_servos: HS's 500 mm / 0.5 kg / SF 1.5 design passed the old payload-only check. With cited Dynamixels and their weight counted (50% of stall, assumed), no Dynamixel X holds the base: it needs 5.66 N m, 1.32 of it from the actuators above it. Shoulder to wrist pick XM540, XM540, XM430, XL430, XL430.
robotic_arm.with_joint_actuators: From the CC BY dataset at 24 V, by rated torque: feasible, 1.43 kg of actuators (base and shoulder 10.5 N m rated units).
robotic_arm.lighter_payload: At 0.2 kg the same arm is feasible with Dynamixels alone: XM540, XM540, XM430, XL430 x3, 0.58 kg of actuators.
robotic_arm.calibration: ROBOTIS rates OpenMANIPULATOR-X (XM430 joints, 380 mm) at 500 g. Stretched, that needs 53% of an XM430's stall torque at the shoulder (58% with its URDF link masses) at SF 1.0. HS's rule (SF 1.5 and 50% of stall) is about 1.6-1.7x stricter than the maker's own rating.
robotic_arm.verdict_change: The arm designer's earlier 'pass' was optimistic; with real parts it now names actuators, mass and where the design breaks.

cctv_rover.drive: 2.5 kg, 80 mm wheels, 2WD, 0.6 m/s, 15 degree slope (rolling resistance 0.03 and 0.3 m/s2 assumed): 17 of 38 Pololu options pass. Lowest current: 25D MP 12V 47:1, 0.68 m/s at cruise, 0.16 A per motor cruising, 0.51 A on the slope.
cctv_rover.camera: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3: Sony IMX708 12 MP, 1080p50, 75 degree diagonal (120 degree Wide), NoIR variants without IR filter, from US$25 (raspberrypi.com product page).
cctv_rover.still_missing: No end-to-end CCTV rover run yet (compute, streaming, battery runtime, chassis).

drone.prop_check: UIUC GWS 3x2 (2-blade, 3 in) at HS-3G's 55.5 g hover thrust: 18,554 rpm, 6.35 W shaft, figure of merit 0.60. HS-3G's 15.26 W per motor hover estimate would mean 42% motor and ESC efficiency on that prop; its 10.06 W upper bound would mean 63%. Neither is ruled out. Lossless motors would cap hover at about 15.7 min, so the 7.1-10.4 min range is physically possible.
drone.verdict_change: Against its real class, HS-3G is on par: same 1404 motors and 4S packs, 7.1 min against 6-8.5 min for the GEPRC quads, heavier (222 g) because it carries GPS, and cheaper than the US$400+ ready-to-fly versions.
